'''Kobe Brown''' (born January 1, 2000) is an American [[college basketball]] player for the [[Missouri Tigers men's basketball|Missouri Tigers]] of the [[Southeastern Conference]] (SEC).

==Early life and high school career==
Brown grew up in [[Huntsville, Alabama]] and attended [[Lee High School (Huntsville, Alabama)|Lee High School]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rocketcitynow.com/article/sports/college/kobe-brown-talks-about-his-freshman-year-at-missouri/525-76fd41ef-9871-41a9-8e6c-2bcae8616665|title=Kobe Brown talks about his freshman year at Missouri|first=Mo|last=Carter|website=[[WZDX|RocketCityNow.com]]|date=April 2, 2020|access-date=March 22, 2023}}</ref> He averaged 20.9 points, 7.9 points and 6.8 assists and was named first team All-State as a junior.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.al.com/recruiting/2018/11/in-state-4-star-gf-kobe-brown-commits-to-sec-west-team.html|title=In-state 4-star G/F Kobe Brown signs with SEC team|first=Daniel|last=Boyette|website=[[AL.com]]|date=November 19, 2018|access-date=March 22, 2023}}</ref> Brown repeated as a first team All-State selection and was named the Huntsville Region Player of the Year after averaging 24.1 points, 12 rebounds, and 8 assists per game during his senior season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.al.com/highschoolsports/2019/03/i-just-had-to-suck-it-up-huntsville-player-of-the-year-kobe-browns-clutch-plays-while-sick-extended-lees-season.html|title=Huntsville Player of the Year Kobe Brown’s clutch plays while sick extended Lee’s season|first=Daniel|last=Boyette|website=[[AL.com]]|date=March 19, 2019|access-date=March 22, 2023}}</ref>

Brown was rated a four-star recruit and initially committed to play college basketball at Texas A&M during his junior year of high school.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://247sports.com/college/texas-am/Article/Texas-AM-basketball-recruiting-AM-lands-versatile-forward-in-Huntsville-Alabama-Kobe-Brown-124710083/|title=BREAKING: A&M basketball lands versatile forward in Kobe Brown|first=Damon|last=Sayles|website=[[247Sports.com]]|date=November 14, 2018|access-date=March 22, 2023}}</ref> He decommitted as a senior and re-opened his recruitment.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.al.com/recruiting/2019/03/texas-am-signee-kobe-brown-of-lee-huntsville-reopens-recruitment.html|title=Texas A&M signee Kobe Brown of Lee-Huntsville reopens recruitment|first=Daniel|last=Boyette|website=[[AL.com]]|date=March 21, 2019|access-date=March 22, 2023}}</ref> Brown ultimately signed to play at Missouri over offers from Minnesota, Penn State, and Vanderbilt.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.kansascity.com/sports/college/sec/university-of-missouri/article230400994.html|title=Kobe Brown, 6-7 forward commits to Mizzou basketball|work=[[The Kansas City Star]]|date=May 14, 2019|access-date=March 22, 2023}}</ref>

==College career==
Brown played in all 30 of the Missouri Tigers' games with 26 starts during his freshman season and averaged 5.8 points and 3.7 rebounds.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.columbiamissourian.com/sports/mizzou_mens_basketball/a-look-at-missouri-mens-basketballs-2020-21-roster-as-it-stands/article_b9b64f82-66d9-11ea-9399-4f99570fcc33.html|title=A look at Missouri men's basketball's 2020-21 roster as it stands|work=[[Columbia Missourian]]|date=March 15, 2020|access-date=March 22, 2023}}</ref> He average eight points and 6.2 rebounds per game as a sophomore.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.columbiamissourian.com/sports/mizzou_mens_basketball/junior-forward-kobe-brown-is-ready-to-be-a-leader/article_bd5b8184-d05f-11eb-8849-cbff2a16a16f.html|title=Junior forward Kobe Brown is ready to be a leader|work=[[Columbia Missourian]]|date=June 18, 2021|access-date=March 22, 2023}}</ref> Brown was named second-team All-[[Southeastern Conference]] (SEC) after leading Missouri with 12.5 points and 7.6 rebounds per game.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.kansascity.com/sports/college/sec/university-of-missouri/article268192337.html|title=Missouri Tigers forward Kobe Brown named preseason All-SEC|work=[[The Kansas City Star]]|date=November 2, 2022|access-date=March 22, 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite
